config.title: Do You Need Restaurant Reservations in Berlin? - FAQ

items.q: Do you need reservations at restaurants in Berlin?
items.a: **Usually not.** Berlin runs on casual, walk-in eating, and for a normal weeknight at a normal neighbourhood restaurant you can simply turn up. Reservations matter for specific cases: **groups of five or more, buzzy or fine-dining places, Friday and Saturday nights, and popular Sunday brunch spots.**

items.q: When should you book a table in Berlin?
items.a: Book when your evening ticks one of these boxes: **a group of five or more, a much-talked-about or Instagram-famous place, a special occasion or tasting menu, or a Friday or Saturday night at a popular restaurant.** For a special meal on a weekend, reserve one to two weeks ahead; for a buzzy spot, two or three days is usually enough.

items.q: Can you just walk into restaurants in Berlin?
items.a: **Yes, most of the time.** The vast majority of Berlin restaurants, cafes and every Imbiss expect walk-ins, and spontaneous eating suits how visitors move through the city. Keep a backup option on the same street in case your first choice is full, and come early for outdoor terraces in summer.

items.q: How do you make a restaurant reservation in Berlin?
items.a: There is no single app. **Start with Google Maps: many Berlin restaurants show a Reserve a table button that books instantly.** If there is none, look for Reservierung on the restaurant's own website, since Berlin's busier kitchens mostly run their own booking widget. **Traditional German restaurants often still take tables by phone or email**, and a short call or a two-line email in plain English almost always works. Plenty of casual places and every Imbiss take no reservations at all.

items.q: Are Berlin restaurants open on Sundays?
items.a: **Many are, but fewer than on a weekday.** Berlin shops mostly close on Sundays, and while plenty of restaurants open, fewer kitchens run and brunch spots get busy. Check a specific place is open before you set out, and treat a popular Sunday brunch like a weekend booking.

items.q: Do you need to book restaurants in Berlin for a large group?
items.a: **Yes. Five or more people is the single biggest reason to reserve anywhere in Berlin.** Large tables are limited, and a full restaurant cannot create one on the spot. Book directly by phone or email, even where online booking exists, ideally a few days ahead.
